This rebases #27629 onto a current mastodon version. This commit is made in the contexts of [discussions](https://www.loomio.com/d/C4HKmTOa/proposal-to-revisit-extending-the-character-limit-for-posts) around increasing the character limit at social.coop.

Modifying a docker container is considerably difficult. Mastodon already has facilities to collapse large posts. It federates with software that has no post limits. Recently, @ClearlyClaire authored https://github.com/mastodon/mastodon/commit/805dba7f8d2a2d5f910ec1396247b36417170345, which means there is only one codepath that needs to be updated. Instance admins modifying source code makes it more prone to breakage. They do it anyway. Splitting up posts disrupts the flow of conversation. It can even be an accessibility concern. 

The cat has left the bag a long time ago. Its time.

Closes #12265

After consideration and discussion across the team: we do not intend to accept a change of this kind for now. Mastodon as it stands today is not intended for authoring long form content. We also feel that the UI does not handle much longer content well enough to remove this restriction today.

We may reconsider this choice in the future. We do have plans to rework the way that Mastodon interacts with long form content, particularly as other platforms join the Fediverse and this area for interoperability continues to grow. This is not a change that we plan to work on as part of our short term roadmap.

Closing as out-of-scope for current plans, but we fully observe the desire of some instance operators to run with an alternative character limit, and Mastodon may make changes to directly support this in the future.

Hi there! I'm part of the admin group of a medium-large instance (~2k active users) and I wanted to chime in with what I believe is representative of part of our community's opinions and questions (although we are a diverse group, so I can't speak for all of https://social.coop).

1. Could you please expand on why you are rejecting PRs that add settings such as this? If you can share, what are the downsides to the project of accepting such settings, in particular given that there *are* many instances out there that go the extra mile to e.g. bump the character limits in Mastodon, or use one of the many other Fediverse servers that support setting arbitrary limits in the first place?
2. Could you please share when the Mastodon project may support higher character limits to your best available estimates? https://social.coop members have expressed a desire to increase this limit, and we are currently exploring options to provision for this preference. If the Mastodon project persists in rejecting PRs like this, we might have to move to a fork like Hometown or consider ditching Mastodon altogether. Both options would cause extra load for our working groups and might disrupt our users, including those who don't particularly care about character limits but would otherwise be completely happy seeing other social.coop members get this feature.
3. More generally: do you have an up to date roadmap published somewhere, or a document detailing which kinds of contributions are likely to be accepted and which are likely to be rejected? I ask this because this is not the first time I see the Mastodon project rejecting a contribution that seems to have substantial community support, and it pains me a bit to see well intended people putting together PRs to be essentially ultimately thrown to Davy Jones' locker :) 

In general, when making these decisions that seem (humbly, to me) to go against user preference, which tradeoffs do you consider? I ask also because, when I browse Mastodon's settings nowadays, I find... many settings which seem quite arcane and like, if they were missing, would have far less user support than a setting to increase post limits (for example). Yet they are there, and there they remain, so I feel like maybe the community is missing further context on how the Mastodon project has evolved over time and what your long term goals look like.

Thank you for your attention, and for developing Mastodon! Have a nice week.

After the recent changes in v4.3 (and the source code consolidation) I was wondering why Mastodon won't let me just configure the MAX_CHARS setting. While I'm not happy with the current situation and would rather like to see a configuration setting, I respect the decision that the Mastodon team has made for the short term. 

Thanks for clarifying, @andypiper !

Let's hope the software can deal with lengthy content better in the future and will provide an easier way to customize the character limit then ;-)

The reason given for not adding MAX_POST_CHARS is that you don't want longer-form content on mastodon.
Ok, fair enough.

But what about making the char limit smaller? Bluesky for example has a 300 char limit and if you're using the Fedi-bridge to post there too, stuff often gets truncated.
Wanting to 'fix' that was the reason I found this dumpster-fire of a discussion.

@andypiper

Also a fair point - this is a (well!) known issue, but not a change that we plan to make in the immediate term. That said, we have started to look at ways to explore longer content display now, in collaboration with other fediverse platforms.

@andypiper Howdy, hachyderm.io infra person here (50k users/10k MAU). At current, we *don't* run a fork/patched version of upstream, but this is the feature we get requested the most often. I don't understand the resistance to making this a configurable setting, but then telling admins "just patch this, that, and this and it works". This seems like a very small PR that provides tangible benefit.

What needs to be true such that these are no longer a concern?

- "Mastodon as it stands today is not intended for authoring long form content."
- "We also feel that the UI does not handle much longer content well enough to remove this restriction today."

Again, while I appreciate that you're considerate of the user experience in the web app, I don't see why you wouldn't accept a simple PR that simplifies the life of admins and provides a feature that is regularly requested.

When the mastodon project reject simple QOL changes like this, it has the effect of discouraging contributors from contributing. This is the *opposite* of what you need to do to be a lasting contender in the social media space.

My goals here are to improve communication on what we're actively working on (which is one reason that [Trunk & Tidbits](https://blog.joinmastodon.org/categories/trunk-and-tidbits/) exists).

What I'm aiming to do on this PR is to provide context and reasoning for why we're not doing this *right now*, and to give the core team space to focus on what they are doing right now. I absolutely do not want to discourage contributions (that is why we rewrote the [contribution guide](https://github.com/mastodon/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)). 

It is clear to me that not everyone is happy with the choice made on this specific PR, which I knew would be the case, but we also have to prioritise our time, and that comes with drawbacks like this. 

I have *huge* appreciation for all of the admins and infra folks running Mastodon instances - Thank You 🙏🏻

<!-- Please use a concise and distinct title for the issue -->

<!-- Consider: Could it be implemented as a 3rd party app using the REST API instead? -->

### Pitch

<!-- Describe your idea for a feature. Make sure it has not already been suggested/implemented/turned down before -->
I found useful to keep the 500 characters limit but many instances are already changed this limits, so why can't we let the admins to easily decide how their istances manage the characters limit.
### Motivation
I love the mastodon microblogs format, the 500 characters limits should be set by default, but the character limits had sense back in 2006, everybody were already typing with a 140 characters limits with mobile phones.
Now in 2019 almost everybody are using whatsapp/telegram/signal without limits.
So this limits has little sense now, another point is I would like to have an instance that give 3 times bigger messages (1000) than actual twitter (who as now increased to 280 but had a little impact on platform) so to attract more people that were put off from twitter because of this limit.

<!-- Why do you think this feature is needed? Who would benefit from it? -->
many instances and many new users should find it more attractive to have a social not so limited on short messages.
nothing will change, just a few users will better articolate some toots, other users will keep writing short toots 
bigger toots will be visible on the first 500 characters so to not change the timeline.
some instances on shared hosting like mine can't really do this change on code so this feature will help to create more instances, 
It'll be useful on educational purposes: schools, universities etc.
will help a lot with youngest that have almost no dea of what was the 140 character limit ;)
Many people are upset with Facebook but they won't jump on mastodon due to writing restrictions.
none of the biggest socials have writing limits (instagram, Facebook, whatsapp, tumblr, snapchat has 1196 limit) so it'll be easier to migrate to mastodon.

There are a few superficial details like this that I think would be great to make admin-customizable. People end up forking the software to modify:

- The post character limit.
- Terms for "post", "boost", and "favorite" in the Notifications.
- Icons for boost and favorite on each post in the timeline.
- The title of the button that publishes posts (which @Gargron called out today re: how he now dislikes calling posts "toots").

It would be great to make all of these easily customizable via the admin interface. The push to be more generic is, I think, to make the software easier for newbies to understand, which makes more sense on larger open-signup instances. For small and closed communities, which are largely people who moved from larger instances to smaller ones, customization is huge for creating your own local flavor.

Plus people would care much less about what the default terms are if different communities can easily change them. :)
